summary.title: Build a multilayer perceptron with Golang
summary.one_liner: You learn how a multilayer perceptron works and how to structure, execute, and train one in Go using backpropagation and gradient descent.
keywords: how to implement neural network from scratch
takeaways: A single perceptron is a binary classifier that cannot separate non-linearly separable classes; stacking layers (input, hidden, output) solves this.
The Go code models Pattern, NeuronUnit, NeuralLayer and MultiLayerNetwork structs, and builds a network from a layer-size slice such as [4, 3, 3].
Execute() propagates inputs forward layer by layer, summing weighted inputs plus bias and applying a transfer function.
BackPropagate() computes output and hidden deltas in reverse order, then updates weights and biases using the learning rate.
MLPTrain() runs backpropagation over the training set for a fixed number of epochs.
summary.summary: The article walks through building a multilayer perceptron from scratch in Go, starting with a brief history of the perceptron (Rosenblatt, 1958) and the limits that led to multilayer networks. It then explains the theory: forward execution, a cost function, gradient descent, and why hidden layers are needed for non-linearly separable problems. The code sections define the core structs (Pattern, NeuronUnit, NeuralLayer, MultiLayerNetwork), show how PrepareMLPNet builds layers, and present the Execute, BackPropagate and MLPTrain functions. The author links to the go-perceptron-go repository for the full example code.
